headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading error: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API outputs can be treated as trusted inputs by a knowledge-management agent with no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a knowledge-management source with no I/O surfaces, while profile B exposes MCP/API/webhook outputs. That creates a plausible bridge where B’s content can be copied into A or downstream workflows and misread as instructions. The pairwise pathway is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF B’s MCP/API output is copied into A’s workspace or notes without provenance labels
IF A is used to summarize or transform B-generated text as if it were trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all B outputs before ingestion
Disable automatic import from B into A
Review one sample B output for instruction-like text before enabling sync
Use a separate workspace for B-derived content
requires-engineering: add source-trust metadata to the integration

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not a meaningful leakage source. B does touch governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data and can call APIs/webhooks, but the pair lacks a shared workspace or shared principal in the profiles. The remaining leakage path is therefore limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF A is manually populated with sensitive notes that are then exported through B
IF B is configured to ingest A-managed files from a shared workspace
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate folders
Restrict B connectors to non-sensitive sources
Audit one export path for accidental inclusion of A content
Turn off webhook destinations not needed today
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write, network, or concurrency surface, so it cannot materially contend for shared mutable resources. B supports multiple instances and can use MCP/API/webhook tooling, but no shared writable target with A is documented. The interaction is therefore possible only under unusual orchestration, with small conflict blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external system
IF B is run in multiple instances against the same connector without locking
mitigations: Assign separate target systems for A and B
Run only one B instance per connector
Check for duplicate writes in one test run
Pause one agent before bulk updates
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a data-catalog/governance agent that can emit metadata through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP, so A’s summaries or curated lists could be treated as authoritative inputs by B or vice versa. A has no verification or action controls in the profile, so a mistaken item can propagate into downstream governance workflows. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF A’s curated content is imported into B as trusted metadata
IF B publishes A-derived records to downstream systems without human review
mitigations: Require human review before B publishes A-derived records
Mark A-derived entries as unverified
Spot-check one lineage record end-to-end
Disable auto-publish for new sources
requires-engineering: add verification gates in the pipeline

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source knowledge-management project with no touched data classes or egress, so it does not itself create a residency or retention mismatch. B touches governance and memory/tribal-knowledge data and has API/webhook surfaces, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated data class or cross-border policy conflict. The compliance risk is therefore limited and indirect.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in B and exported into A-managed artifacts
IF B is configured with a retention policy that differs from the operator’s policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B today
Review retention settings in B
Delete any accidental sensitive test records
Document the data class allowed in each system
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
